title: The Bonnie Situation: How Giving Arthropods Names Can Improve Perception at Outreach Events
content: The barriers to building an entomology outreach program can be relatively low (Madalinska and Monzon 2025), but we often do not critically evaluate which techniques work best for engaging broad audiences, changing perceptions, or encouraging learning at our events. For many of us, Cornell drawers, insect specimens, and mini-museums can help us engage with libraries and schools (Carruthers et al. 2025, Herrera-Motta 2025, Wooden 2023). Bringing live insects to out-reach events can make exhibits feel more alive. This approach also helps attendants connect more deeply with the specimens they see behind the glass, fostering stronger conservation efforts (Herbison 2025). However, we still know relatively little about how to best reach our goals and communicate effectively with the general public regarding our field.
